test_title: PYST 34: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - Mathematics (Held On: 19 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: What will be the difference in population 3 years ago and 2 years ago of a town whose current population of 2,60,000 is increasing at a rate of 25% every year?
solution:
**Given:**

Current population (P) = 2,60,000

Rate of increase (r) = 25% = 25/100 = 0.25

Time 3 years ago (t1) = 3 years

Time 2 years ago (t2) = 2 years

**Formula used:**

Population t years ago = P / (1 + r)t

**Calculations:**

Population 3 years ago:

⇒ Population = 2,60,000 / (1 + 0.25)³

⇒ Population = 2,60,000 / (1.25)³

⇒ Population = 2,60,000 / 1.953125

⇒ Population = 1,33,120

Population 2 years ago:

⇒ Population = 2,60,000 / (1 + 0.25)²

⇒ Population = 2,60,000 / (1.25)²

⇒ Population = 2,60,000 / 1.5625

⇒ Population = 1,66,400

Difference in population:

⇒ Difference = Population 2 years ago - Population 3 years ago

⇒ Difference =1,66,400 - 1,33,120

⇒ Difference = 33,280

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**
